mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT rose monotonically from -55.3 to -41.9 percent across the four weekly means; transit recovery enlarges the pool of non-home trips and, with a three-to-four week lag, lifts RETAIL_REC above its current -19.6 four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved every week from -55.3 to -41.9
failure_condition: The 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC after the decision point is equal to or below the prior 28-day mean (-19.6) while TRANSIT keeps rising above -41.9.

mechanism_narrative: Once the TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -45 percent, trip capacity is sufficient for discretionary outings; RETAIL_REC then rises over the following two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers return to stores.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -45 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT crossed -45 at t-1w (-44.6) and held at t-0w (-41.9)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the two weeks following the week in which TRANSIT first prints above -45 percent.

mechanism_narrative: The joint move - RESIDENTIAL falling from +10.7 to +5.1 while WORKPLACES recovers from -23.9 to -15.1 - marks households reallocating time out of the home; only the interaction predicts higher RETAIL_REC, since either series alone is too noisy.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean at or below +6 while WORKPLACES weekly mean is at or above -16
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from +10.7 to +5.1 while WORKPLACES recovered to -15.1
failure_condition: Weeks where both conditions hold show no increase in RETAIL_REC two weeks later compared with weeks where neither holds.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week PARKS drop of five points or more, as in the move from -14.9 to -22.4 at t-0w, reflects a late-winter cold snap that suppresses all out-of-home activity; RETAIL_REC follows downward within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls at least 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -14.9 at t-1w to -22.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a PARKS week-on-week decline of five points or more.

mechanism_narrative: Under an easing-restrictions regime, sustained TRANSIT gains and RESIDENTIAL below +6 translate directly into retail footfall because permitted trip types widen; the same two signals do not lift RETAIL_REC when restrictions are tightening.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean above -50 and RESIDENTIAL weekly mean below +6 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT above -50 and RESIDENTIAL below +6 in both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In easing-regime weeks, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is no higher than in tightening-regime weeks with the same TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL readings.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL holding at or above +5 percent baseline indicates persistent home-anchored routines; while it persists, discretionary retail trips stay suppressed and RETAIL_REC does not recover from its -16 to -18 plateau.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays at or above +5 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL held at +5.1, +5.7, +5.1 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week in weeks where RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +5.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM converging toward baseline (-7.9 to -4.6) removes stockpiling-driven essential trips, while rising TRANSIT re-routes that same trip capacity to discretionary destinations; the combination raises RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean above -5 while TRANSIT weekly mean rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -7.9 to -4.6 while TRANSIT rose from -55.3 to -41.9
failure_condition: Weeks combining GROCERY_PHARM above -5 with two consecutive TRANSIT gains show RETAIL_REC falling over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES oscillates between -15 and -24 without holding above -20; a relapse below -20 signals that employer office-return policy is stalling, which starves weekday retail footfall and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean falls back below -20 after having printed above -16
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES alternated -15.4, -23.9, -15.1 across the last three weeks
failure_condition: After a WORKPLACES relapse below -20 following a reading above -16, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or higher than the prior 28-day mean.
